sentences.text: This section describes how helitack and ground crews receive assignments, staging information, hazards, and updated intelligence from the support system during active wildfire operations.
When a held recommendation is cleared, the Air Attack Supervisor selects the operational intent in the Caldera Incident Command Portal.
The Caldera Incident Command Portal records each assignment package with an objective, time validity, confirmation status, and required acknowledgments.
The Crewline Mobile Tablet displays the current division assignment, route guidance, rally location, and assigned communications channel for the logged-in crew.
The Helitack Crew Leader receives the same operational package with aviation constraints and landing zone notes after Air Attack Supervisor approval.
Ground crew assignments are formatted for field execution and avoid analytic scores that are not needed for tactical movement.
Staging information is maintained as georeferenced areas and route descriptions so that crews can confirm location without relying on informal landmarks.
The Crewline Mobile Tablet caches the latest accepted staging information and marks any expired package as unavailable for execution.
If the Confirmed Ignition State changes the perimeter or priority area, the Caldera Incident Command Portal marks affected crew assignments for review before release.
The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine updates hazard summaries when fire spread estimates, access constraints, or field observations change.
The Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine applies the Ridge Shadow Mask when estimating crew-visible fire edge confidence in steep terrain.
The Smoke Classifier Module uses the Camera Cleaning Log to suppress confidence changes caused by lens contamination and service timing.
Lantern issues a crew exposure refresh only after the current reconnaissance confidence and weather timing fields are both valid.
Hazards shown to crews include unstable snags, limited access, steep slope exposure, utility conflicts, and escape route degradation.
The MesoWest Weather Fusion Node provides weather-derived exposure flags that support staging decisions near ridgelines and drainages.
When the system enters the Airspace Restricted State, helitack assignments show the restriction boundary and require confirmation before aircraft-dependent movement is planned.
The Drone Tasking Service maintains reconnaissance task status so that ground teams can see whether requested intelligence is pending, active, or complete.
Horizon Ridge Drone Dock status is shown as an availability input only and does not by itself authorize crew movement into a new area.
The Drone Pilot Operator confirms launch readiness separately from crew assignment acceptance to keep reconnaissance execution independent from ground deployment.
The VHF Radio Gateway Repeater mirrors priority assignment summaries for crews that cannot maintain a data session in canyon or timbered terrain.
If the data link is degraded, the Crewline Mobile Tablet presents the last verified assignment package and clearly identifies the time of last update.
The Helitack Crew Leader acknowledges assignment receipt, reports readiness, and records any exception that prevents safe execution.
The County Emergency Liaison can view staging posture and public safety implications without gaining authority to alter crew assignments or hazard records.
All assignment and staging changes preserve an audit trail so that later reviews can reconstruct what information was available to each crew at the time of action.
